implementation.reason: Remove only the cancellation check at the start of each pending-entry iteration. Coherent read ports and plain envelopes cannot change queue identity/generation. All eight post-delivery checkpoints, per-entry clock reads, entry guard and finally cleanup remain.

conclusion: Waiting-queue batches use 8.9–14.3% less CPU than the initial SDK in these four desktop runs (about 6.7–12.7 ns per drain). They remain 9.1–24.3% above the predecessor. Dense and filtered delivery rankings vary with run/order; no broad delivery or whole-game speed improvement is established. Empty-path changes also vary despite no removed work executing for an empty queue. All retained heap medians remain about 176–178 bytes per entry.
scope: Two repeated default-order runs and two supplemental first-execution-order diagnostics. Eight warmups and 25 rotating samples per graph per workload; three separately loaded game graphs. Only graph order/metadata handling changed in the supplemental helper; module import order stayed fixed. These are not balanced factorial replications and do not isolate order from all process/run variation. No rendered FPS, Steam Deck/mobile acceptance, total allocations, peak-memory or normal-queue capacity claim.
